utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-95-10-I, the Prosecutor versus Ranko Cesic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good afternoon to everyone. May I first have the appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. My name is Mark Harmon. To my right is Mr. Vladimir Tochilovsky, and to his right is Mr. Tom Hannis, and to my left is Susan Grogan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harmon. May I have the appearances for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you -- MR. V. NEDIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour and my learned friends, I'm Vojislav Nedic, attorney-at-law from Belgrade. Mr. Ranko Cesic has appointed me his Defence attorney. My professional career goes back 25 years and, in essence, it may be divided into two parts. In the first part, I was a Judge --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Nedic, I will easily accept that you have an outstanding career. I don't think that at this very moment we need any further information about that. So you are Mr. Nedic, and next to you is sitting -- I think both your names are Nedic. MR. V. NEDIC: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just in order to -- one of you is Vojislav Nedic. That's you. MR. V. NEDIC: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And next to you is Radoslav Nedic? Yes. Well, thank you very much. We will proceed today with the initial appearance of the accused Ranko Cesic. Let me first ask you - I'd forgotten - but can you hear me, Mr. Cesic, in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. May I ask you a few questions? First, could you please give your full name for the record. Yes. We have technical problems, as far as I -- it might -- Yes. Do you now understand the interpretation of what I'm saying? Yes. Mr. Cesic, could you please give your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Ranko Cesic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have any nicknames or is this the name always used?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only my name is used. I have no special nickname.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you tell us your date of birth.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] September 1964.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I didn't hear what date in September, but I might not have listened well. Which day in September?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 5th of September, 1964.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. What was the last address you resided on before you were transferred to the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Vinogradska Street 35D in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cesic, have you received a copy of the indictment in a language you understand, and have you read it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I have received it, and I have read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were you able to discuss the content of the indictment with counsel?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I then take it that you understand the content of it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cesic, at this initial appearance, you're entitled to plead, in respect of this indictment, guilty or not guilty to each count, but you also may do it at a later stage. Have you consulted with your counsel whether you'd enter your pleas today or at a later stage?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have decided to enter my pleas today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I was informed - but counsel would correct me if I'm not well informed - that the accused waived his right to have the indictment read out loudly in its entirety. That is true? So Mr. Cesic, I do understand that you waived your right to have read out your indictment in its full text. So we'll just refer to the individual counts when we continue. We are talking about the second amended indictment, which is not only pertaining to you but also to someone who has already stood trial here in The Hague, Mr. Jelesic. You have been arrested on the basis of a warrant of arrest which was issued on the 18th of April in 2001. And may I invite you to, on each count that you plead, plead guilty or not guilty, and I'll confront you with each of these counts. The numbers are the numbers as they appear in the indictment, and therefore we do not start with number 1. Count 2 charges you with the murder of five persons that was allegedly committed in May 1992 and it charges you with this murder as a violation of the laws or customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty to that count?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Count 3 charges you - and that is cumulatively - with the same but now characterised as crimes against humanity. Do you plead guilty or do you plead not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Count 24 of the indictment charges you with the murder of a person with the name Sejdo in May 1992 as a violation of the laws and the customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Count 25 of the indictment charges you, again cumulatively, with the murder of the same person, Sejdo, but now as a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Count 26 charges you with the murder of Mirsad Glavovic in May 1992 as a violation of the laws and customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I didn't understand the translation well. But it's --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Count 27 charges you, again cumulatively, with the same murder of Mirsad Glavovic but now characterised as a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Count 28 of the indictment charges you with the humiliation and degrading treatment of two persons in May 1992 as a violation of the laws or customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Count 29 charges you with the same acts but now characterised as rape, which includes other forms of sexual assault, as a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Count 34 of the indictment charges you with the murder of Nijad Jasarevic in May 1992 as a violation of the laws or customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Count 35 charges you cumulatively with the same murder but now characterised as a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Count 42 of the indictment charges you with the murder of two unknown men in May 1992 as a violation of the laws or customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Count 43 charges you, again cumulatively, with the same murders, characterised now as a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. Madam Registrar, will you please take note that Mr. Cesic has pleaded not guilty to all the counts in his respect in the indictment. The Registrar will be instructed to fix a date, although it might not be appropriate to do it right away, but will at a later stage fix a date for trial. And you, Mr. Cesic, you will have to remain in custody until further order in the detention facilities of the UN here in The Hague. Is there any specific matter the Prosecution would like to raise at this very moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, there is not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is not. Thank you, Mr. Harmon. Is there any matter the Defence would like to raise at this very moment? MR. V. NEDIC: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me then ask you, Mr. Cesic, is everyone who should be informed about your presence here in the Tribunal at this moment, is he or she informed? I mean your family or the diplomatic agency representing your country in The Hague. Is everyone aware of your presence here or is there any specific need to inform specific people about your presence here?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They have all been informed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So, then, no specific action is necessary to be taken in that respect. As far as your detention as such is concerned - and I'm not asking just of you but perhaps also an answer could be given by your counsel - are there any specific issues in respect of the arrest, transfer, or detention which should be raised at this moment? MR. V. NEDIC: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There is not. Please be seated, Mr. Cesic. Then I may remind the Prosecution that they have obligations under Rule 66 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence to disclose within 30 days all the supporting material to the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If I may comment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We will disclose today the supporting material in a language the accused understands, today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We will disclose eight witness statements to the accused, seven of which are translated in a language that he understands. We have two expert reports that we will be filing very shortly in this case as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So your disclosure obligations are taken very seriously not only as far as the content is concerned but also as far as the time limits are concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would like to file any preliminary motions, you will have to do that within 30 days, 30 days from the moment that you have received all of the supporting material, in accordance with the Rules. So it's not from this date but as soon as you have received all the supporting material. I take it that if it's given in portions, that you indicate clearly at what moment all the supporting material has been provided to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We will provide all of the supporting material today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's today.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So your 30 days' time limit starts today, at least if later on today you receive all the supporting material. I further inform you that a Status Conference will be scheduled within 120 days, a Status Conference which serves an expeditious preparation of the case. Is there anything else you would like to address the Court? MR. V. NEDIC: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The same for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: We have nothing further, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I will adjourn the proceedings at this moment until further order.
